reason: There are two statements here. 'Many flowered' is an indefinite count of flowers per inflorescence, which is pattern 13. 'Laxly' is the loose arrangement of the inflorescence (PATO_0001802 loose, related synonym lax, as in the previous rule C169).
Covered with scales means scaly, as lepidote was in rule C235. 'Densely' is a degree that stays in the record, and 'at base' or 'towards apex' goes to the region slot.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (part of the bearer): bearer pubescent (PATO_0000455) + its trichome (PO_0000282) brown (PATO_0000952)
reason: This combines two values. The brown colour belongs to the hairs, not to the organ, so it should become 'organ pubescent' plus 'hairs of the organ brown' rather than one new term.

This is the transcriber's attribute heading, not a quality. The statements behind it (e.g. 'covering the outer stamens') are relations to another part and belong to docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md.

target: lobe of the stated organ: corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006), calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005), perianth lobe (FLOPO_0986004); quality length (PATO_0000122)
reason: This is a length measurement whose bearer is the lobe, not the named organ, so the measurement should move to the lobe class. No lobe class exists for leaf laminas or receptacles, so those statements stay unresolved.

target: corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006), calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005), perianth lobe (FLOPO_0986004); quality length (PATO_0000122)
reason: Same as 'length of lobes'. The measured part is the lobe of the corolla, calyx or perianth. Lobes of lemmas, bracts and stigmas have no class.

For whole plants, 'crown' is the tree crown, which PO lists as a synonym of shoot system; 'dense', 'rounded' and 'spreading' then describe that bearer. The crown on ovaries, flowers and lemmas is a different sense (coronate, FLOPO:0991315).

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md: distance (PATO_0000040) towards the base of the named part, with magnitude and unit
reason: '1–2.3 mm from the base of the tube' measures where a part is inserted relative to a landmark on another part. Distance is relational in PATO, so this needs the 'towards' slot and a number, not a term.

A minute abrupt point at the apex is a mucronulate apex, and the floras use the two words as alternatives ('minutely apiculate or mucronulate'). PATO has 'apiculate' only as a synonym of the attribute sharpness (PATO_0000944), which cannot be used as a value.
Flavous is the Latin-derived word for yellow, the same as luteous. It goes to the yellow class of the colour backbone, as other colour synonyms in config/botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv do.
Rostrate is an exact synonym of beaked. 'Obliquely' only gives the beak's angle on a moss operculum (spore capsule operculum PO_0030044), so it stays as a qualifier and no new term is needed.
Anthela is an inflorescence type in PO, so this is a bearer, not a quality. PO has no compound-inflorescence class, so 'compound' is kept as words in the record.

label: leptosporangiate
definition: A structural quality inhering in a sporangium by virtue of its developing from a single superficial initial cell and having a wall one cell layer thick, usually on a slender stalk.
reason: This is a real botanical sporangium type with no PATO term and no PO leptosporangium class. It is the opposite of eusporangiate. It is mostly constant within fern orders, so it tells little within a flora.

target: calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005) for calyx teeth; quality length (PATO_0000122)
reason: The length belongs to the teeth, and calyx teeth are calyx lobes. Teeth of leaf margins, involucres and fruit beaks have no class, and those statements should stay unresolved rather than go to the organ.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (part of the bearer): margin of the stated organ (leaf margin PO_0020128 for leaves) + ciliated (PATO_0001408, the pipeline's current grounding of 'ciliate')
reason: The quality is ciliate and 'margins' is the region of the bearer, so this is the margin slot plus a quality, not a new term. PATO_0001408 is defined as a cell quality (having cilia), so a botanical 'ciliate' value deserves its own review.
A corona on a corolla throat or hypanthium is the floral corona, a part. 'Hojas en corona' (leaves in a crown) is a different sense, a rosette (FLOPO:0991005), and should not follow this rule.
An unfringed ligule or wing has a margin without a fringe, which is the negation of fringed.

Silicula and silicle are synonyms of silique fruit in PO, so this is a fruit type, i.e. a bearer. The short-versus-long distinction is a length-to-width ratio (docs/odp/11-ratio-of-two-dimensions.md).
This states that a style is present ('with styles') or absent ('estilo ausente'). The absent case is docs/odp/15-absence-of-a-part.md, and 'with or without styles' is a pair of alternatives.
The surface is marked with minute dark dots like grains of sand, which is punctate. The text does not say the dots are glands, so gland-dotted (FLOPO:0991174) would claim too much.
Papillate is an exact synonym of papillose, so this is its negation.
This is a transcription fragment of 'tri- to tetrapinnatilobate' and 'tri- to plurifoliate'. The whole phrase is a count of parts (docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md) with alternatives.

The stem or plant is branched, and 'from base' is the region (base, as for the context word 'at base' in config/flora_context_words.tsv). Branched plus region covers it, so no 'basally branched' term is needed.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (decreased length PATO_0000574 towards the tube of the calyx or corolla)
reason: This compares a length with a named second part, which is the example wording of pattern 09. The lone 'shorter' was rejected in the previous review only because it lacked the second part.

Leaves uniformly distributed along the stem are separated by about equal distances, which is the definition of evenly spaced. PATO's 'uniform' (PATO_0000438, invariant) is about not varying, not about spacing.

A dibrachiate hair has two arms on either side of its point of attachment (a malpighian or T-shaped hair). That is the medifixed definition, which already has 'medifixed hair' and 'malpighian' as related synonyms.
Made wider is dilated, as 'expanded' was in rule C181. 'At base' goes to the region slot.
'Soon decaying' bracts and bracteoles fall or wither very early, which is fugacious. 'Sheaths decaying to fibers' is a different meaning (breaking down into fibres) and should not follow this rule.
